doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Coltrane's influence, range of experience and tenor sound
summary: Cobb and Booker say later saxophonists struggle after Coltrane; Cobb lists his bands and says he played alto until he heard Parker.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Now everybody, I feel sorry for the saxophone players that have to come behind that one. Because say, whoa, wait a minute, I got to learn all of this?

Yeah, learn that, in the hopes that something will come out of him, you know. And that’s probably why they want to go in other directions. So they go no I don’t think so and they go and they try to skip over that see? They usually did that, they preferred to skip over that, they’ll say we’ll have his sound and then we’ll go and do, but his sound was all that it was.

Yeah he had a whole lot of experience. He did a whole lot of things. You know he played in all kinds of bands, he played in funk bands, he played bebop, he played in big bands, he played in Jimmy Heath’s band when Jimmy Heath had a band in Philadelphia, and he played alto, you know, until he heard Charlie Parker, then he stopped doing that.
Some people say that he played the tenor so high because he really still heard the sounds from the alto, like he was playing everything a fourth up higher.
He probably felt more comfortable up there, not because of his knowledge, just because of his ears, and what made him feel comfortable, you know?
